Package com.bilt.pos.widget

package com.bilt.pos.widget
Contracts between a Bilt widget and the register screen it draws on.

A widget (the retail-media banner is the first) decides what to show and when; the register decides where. The seam between the two is Surface: the widget hands a Rendering to the surface, the surface draws it and reports the shopper's interactions back through the ActionSink it was given. Nothing in a rendering carries PII; a rendering is a structured creative — media, copy, up to two calls to action with opaque tokens, a TTL and tracking URLs — that any surface can draw.

Surface tiers

Registers differ wildly in what they can host, so the SDK offers five ways to get a rendering on screen, from least to most integration work for the register:

  1. Hand us a container. A platform module supplies a native adapter — an Android View, a Compose slot, a Swing panel — that implements Surface and draws the rendering with platform widgets. The register only reserves the space.
  2. Hand us a WebView. The register already embeds a browser control; it subclasses WebSurface, wires two calls (loadUrl and evaluateJavascript) and one inbound JavaScript interface, and the SDK drives Bilt's hosted renderer page through a small, documented JSON bridge.
  3. Hand us a URL slot. The register can point an iframe or kiosk browser at a URL but cannot script it; the SDK gives it a hosted page URL bound to the session and the page talks to Bilt directly. Interactions reach the SDK through the ad platform's event channel rather than a local sink.
  4. Take the content. The register wants to draw the creative in its own design system; it receives the Rendering itself (media URLs, copy, CTA tokens) and draws whatever it likes, reporting interactions through the sink like any other surface.
  5. Implement Surface yourself. Anything else — a second cashier display, a pin-pad line, a receipt footer — is a Surface implementation the register owns end to end.

This core module is platform-neutral: it defines the contracts and the web bridge but ships no adapter. Adapters live in the platform modules, next to the UI toolkit they draw with.

Threading

The widget calls a surface from its own single-threaded executor; a surface marshals to its UI thread as needed and must never block the caller. Callbacks into the ActionSink may arrive from any thread, including a UI or JavaScript thread; the sink marshals back to the widget.
